title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol: cannot love unless reconciled — slippery and false; loves to gift faith
pass_a_gloss: The things which are attached, namely, that God cannot in the aforesaid manner love anyone unto salvation unless reconciled; but cannot be reconciled to anyone except from antecedent foresight of his faith, are very slippery, nay manifestly false. For by this love, which is understood to lie hidden in the decree of election, God loves one not yet reconciled so far as to appoint him to be reconciled to himself; he loves one not yet faithful so far as to decree him to be gifted with faith: although he does not love in that manner in which he loves his sons already adopted, reconciled, and believing.
pass_b_english: What they attach — that God cannot so love anyone unto salvation unless reconciled, and cannot be reconciled to anyone except from antecedent foresight of his faith — is very slippery, indeed plainly false. By the love latent in the election decree, God loves one not yet reconciled so far as to appoint him to be reconciled; loves one not yet faithful so far as to decree him gifted with faith — though not as he loves sons already adopted, reconciled, and believing.
source_text: Quae attexuntur, scilicet, Deum non posse praedicto modo ad salutem amare quenquam nisi reconciliatum; reconciliari autem non posse cuiquam nisi ex antecedanea fidei ejus praevisione, sunt valde lubrica, imo manifeste falsa. Nam hoc amore, qui in electionis decreto latere intelligitur, Deus amat nondum reconciliatum eatenus ut illum sibi reconciliandum statuat; amat nondum fidelem, eatenus ut eum fide donandum decernat: quamvis non eo modo amet quo filios suos jam adoptatos, reconciliatos et credentes.
